cars.variant: SS Sport Coupe RPO 587 dual-carb 409 — 1962 USA factory reference, four-speed
cars.specification_market: 1962 USA Impala SS Sport Coupe with optional RPO 587 dual-carb 409 and selected four-speed manual. Engine ratings January 1962 revision; component details April revision. Preserve explicit gross rating and native units. No default Positraction, axle ratio, racing modification, body mass or measured performance assumed. Count the 1961–1964 Impala performance-road family once across engines, years and bodies; the existing 1994–1996 SS is separate.
cars.summary: The early Impala SS 409 is an American performance and cultural icon: the optional dual-quad big-block paired serious factory road-car hardware with the Super Sport coupe, while the 409 name became part of popular music. Chevrolet’s history explicitly connects the early SS programme with the 1962 Beach Boys song.

sources.notes: Selected RPO 587 dual-four-barrel 409, not single-carb RPO 580. Printed POWER TRAINS 27 rates 409 brake GROSS hp at 6000 and 420 gross lb-ft at 4000; no modern net or kW conversion. Ratings leaf revised January 1962; component/cooling leaves revised April 1962. Performance-weight table concerns model 1669 with passenger allowance, not this coupe curb weight; calculated axle examples are not an assigned ratio. Engine identification page predates the revised dual-carb rating; no suffix inferred.

sources.notes: SS panel at PDF index 3 explicitly offers Super Sport equipment on Sport Coupe and convertible, with optional V8 engines up to 409 hp and optional four-speed Synchro-Mesh. SS trim alone does not imply a 409, Positraction or every heavy-duty option. Bucket seats/locking console mapped here, not inferred from secondary option-price summaries.
